# Independently specified viewport evidence

The ASCII `reference-perspective.dxf` is hand-specified from DXF group meanings,
not generated by opencadcodec. Its axial and oblique cameras and landmark
constants are recorded in `reference-perspective.json`.

The test calculation derives from [Autodesk's WCS/DCS perspective matrix](https://blog.autodesk.io/setting-the-view-center-in-an-external-dwg-file-with-objectarx-or-realdwg-in-c/comment-page-1/)
(Fenton Webb, 2012). For aspect a, Model view height h and lens m, adjusted lens
L = h*m*sqrt(1+a*a)/42. Camera distance d is the direction norm. After inverse
target/basis/twist/pan transformation, homogeneous w=(d-z)/L. Paper coordinates
scale projected XY by Paper height/h, then add the frame centre. The helper is
test-only; no new production projection API exists.

The axial expected offsets follow F=100*50*sqrt(3.56)/42 and F*10/(100-z).
For the oblique direction [60,0,80], the untwisted axes are [0,1,0],
[-0.8,0,0.6], [0.6,0,0.8]. Rotate the first two axes by negative PI/6 before
subtracting DCS centre [5,-3]. Its Paper focal value is
80*35*sqrt(3.25)/42. These expressions establish the stored landmark constants
independently of the codec and converter. Signed depth clips use target-relative
view Z: back -20 <= z <= front -10. Comparisons allow 1e-10 Paper coordinate units
for external-reference arithmetic only; native conversion precision is unchanged.

This is documented reference-calculation evidence, not an AutoCAD-produced
fixture or certification of rendered pixels. Cases are checked through literal
DXF loading and production DXF/DWG exchange, with mm, inch and unitless Model
coordinates. Lens lengths remain millimetres.

The independent 30-degree DXF twist exposed omitted degree/radian conversion in
the pinned codec. Local patch 0002 repairs groups 50/51. [Autodesk's group-code
reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm)
documents file degrees versus API radians. The separate viewport-off regression
uses literal group 90 value 229376 (0x8000 | 0x10000 | 0x20000), proving the explicit
off bit survives decoding independently of the historically named `is_on` bit.

`reference-clip-activation.dxf` is likewise hand-specified: group 90=98304 and
group 340=1002, referring forward to a Circle. It isolates the clipping reader
regression; full structured documents exercise actual codec roundtrips.
